validUntil.description:
ValidUntil is the scheduler's heartbeat: the status holds until then.
Past it (or absent), the core isn't responding.

setupLeft.description:
SetupLeft names the setup steps still to do (`setup --json`'s titles;
empty when setup is done). Unfinished setup makes health error.

pendingAcknowledgements.description:
PendingAcknowledgements is how many notifications wait for me to
acknowledge them (Waiting's length); any makes health error.

items.description: Waiting is a notification waiting for me to acknowledge it.

waiting.description:
Waiting are those notifications (`notifications list --waiting`),
oldest first.

busy.description:
Busy is true while a routine is running (not counting runs stuck past
MaxRunDuration); frontends show activity from it.

summary.description:
Summary is the state in a few words ("All good", "No routines
enabled"), for frontends to show when there are no reasons.

problem.description:
Problem says why the scheduler can't work right now (e.g. the config
file doesn't load); set and cleared by the scheduler on every check.

Problem says why the routine can't be scheduled (e.g. its file doesn't
parse). It's current state, cleared as soon as the routine is fixed. A
hook's ends with what's wrong with its watcher, when something is:
"its watcher " and WatcherProblem.

watcher.description:
Watcher is the watcher a hook listens to, and WatcherProblem what's
wrong with it that keeps the hook from hearing its events (failing,
untrusted, paused, a permission it needs), said about the watcher
("keys is failing: …"): the same for every hook on it, so it's one
reason, about the watcher, not one per hook.

healthResetAt.description:
HealthResetAt is when the scheduler last found that a permission it
needs changed (its state, or which ones it needs): a run that started
before then no longer counts toward its health, which is none until it
runs again. Its runs stay in history as they were.

nextRunAt.description:
NextRunAt is the next slot the scheduler will handle (enabled, scheduled
routines only). The scheduler moves it forward as soon as it picks a slot
up, so one more than SchedulerGrace in the past means it didn't.

trigger.description:
Trigger is what started the run: "schedule", "manual", "backfill" or
(a hook's) "event" (empty in records from before triggers were
recorded).

for.description: For is the time the run is for (the schedule slot, the backfilled day).

id.description: ID is the run's history ID (as `runs show` takes).

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the run's saved agent CLI session (routines with
session: save): set when the run starts if the app picks its ID, when
it ends if the CLI does (Backend says which CLI resumes it).

backend.description:
Backend is the model backend running it, or that ran it (llm.backend's
value), once it got as far as the model.

folder.description:
Folder is the folder the run worked in (where its session resumes
from), unless it was an empty temporary one.

deadline.description: Deadline is when a running run is stopped (its routine's timeout).

queuedAt.description: QueuedAt is when the run started waiting for its turn, if it had to.

health.description:
Health is the routine's own verdict: error when it makes the app's
health error, ok while it's enabled and fine, none while it's paused
or, after a health reset, until it runs again.

summary.description:
Summary is its state in a few words ("Next: tomorrow 09:20", "standup
failed", "Paused"), for frontends to show as is.

problem.description:
Problem says why the routine can't be scheduled (e.g. its file doesn't
parse). It's current state, cleared as soon as the routine is fixed. A
hook's ends with what's wrong with its watcher, when something is:
"its watcher " and WatcherProblem.

hooks.description:
Hooks are the hooks, as routines are: each with its last run, its
health and summary. A hook is never among Routines.

routine.description: Routine it's about; empty for the scheduler itself.

hook.description: Hook is true when Routine names a hook, not a routine.

watcher.description:
Watcher is the watcher it's about, when what's wrong is a watcher's
(failing, untrusted, paused, a permission it needs): one reason for
it, naming the hooks that listen to it, and Routine is empty.

text.description:
Text is a short headline ("standup failed"); Detail the full story (the
run's reason), for frontends to show on demand.

run.description: Run is the run it's about (a history ID, as `runs show` takes), if any.

acknowledge.description:
Acknowledge is true when it's about notifications waiting for me to
acknowledge them: choosing it shows them (`notifications list
--waiting`), to acknowledge.

items.description: Reason is one thing making health error.

reasons.description:
Reasons say why health is error, in words, for frontends to show as
they are; empty when it isn't. They come from the same rules as health.

title: Run status
description: Written by the Go core, watched by frontends: Status is the whole record.
